# v0.49.72

This patch stops a search from sending a project's whole memory store to the embedding provider at once, and stops effort changes from rewriting the prompt cache on newer Claude models.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Search sent every memory to the embedding provider at once (#957, thanks @iceteaSA):** after stored memory vectors were lost, for example after changing the embedding model, a search with no keyword match embedded every memory that had no vector in a single request. On a large project that request timed out or tripped the provider's failure guard. A search now embeds at most 50 such memories, in requests of at most 10, chosen in a fixed order. The rest are still found by keyword, and the background job fills in their vectors as before.
- **Effort changes rewrote the prompt cache on newer Claude models:** changing the reasoning effort mid-session made Magic Context rebuild the request on Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.1 and Mythos 5.2, and on Opus 5.5 when reached through Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex. These models carry the effort change without touching the cached prompt, so the rebuild was the only cost. They now keep their cache, as Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 already did. Older models are unchanged.

# v0.49.71

This patch fixes the docs upkeep maintenance task, which failed on every run for projects whose docs have subsections.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Docs upkeep failed on nested sections (#963, thanks @mgt-l):** the task treated every heading as the end of the section above it, so a section's `###` subsections didn't count as part of its `##` section. When the model proposed an update to a whole `##` section, including its subsections, the check refused it. One refused entry then discarded the whole proposal, and the task never moved past it, so it failed the same way on every run. A section now runs from its heading to the next heading of the same or a higher level (headings inside code blocks don't count). Replacing or removing a `##` section includes its subsections, and protected regions are still kept byte for byte. Each proposed change is now checked on its own: an invalid one is dropped with its reason recorded, the valid ones are kept, and the run completes and moves on.

# v0.49.70

This patch fixes summaries on Oh My Pi 19.1 and two `doctor` gaps for Pi and Oh My Pi users.

## Upgrading

Update with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest`. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Summaries failed on Oh My Pi 19.1:** Oh My Pi 19.1.0 switches on its Auto-QA issue reporter in every run, including Magic Context's hidden summary and maintenance runs, which ask for no tools. Magic Context refuses any hidden run that has a tool, so on 19.1.0 every summary failed, and long sessions could end up refusing turns. Hidden runs on Oh My Pi now turn Auto-QA off with Oh My Pi's own setting. Your own Oh My Pi sessions and plain Pi are unchanged.
- **`doctor --fix` now repairs Pi (#961, thanks @VibePDF):** `--fix` never reached the Pi doctor, so only `--force` could repair a Pi install. `--fix` now repairs Pi's config and clears stale extension caches, and `--force` clears them even when they look current. Before clearing, the doctor now checks that no running Pi or Oh My Pi still has those files or Magic Context's database open. If one does, it leaves the cache alone and names the process to quit. If it can't check, it refuses, as it already did for OpenCode.
- **Oh My Pi users get the real upgrade path (#961):** the doctor can't change the plugin Oh My Pi has installed. With `--fix` or `--force` it now says how to upgrade: run `omp plugin install @cortexkit/pi-magic-context@latest`, then restart running Oh My Pi sessions. Config repairs for Oh My Pi still need `--force`.

# v0.49.69

This patch stops the reduce reminders from asking the agent to drop conversation it was told to keep.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Reduce reminders counted conversation as reclaimable (#954, thanks @iceteaSA):** the "Hygiene" reading in the sidebar, and the reminders built on it, counted your messages and the agent's own replies as something the agent could reduce. The `ctx_reduce` guidance tells the agent to keep exactly that text, so on a session that is mostly conversation the reading stayed high however well the agent reduced, and the reminders kept asking for reductions it isn't allowed to make. Conversation now counts toward the total but not toward what is reclaimable; tool output and files still do. This applies on OpenCode and Pi alike.

# v0.49.68

This patch fixes two OpenCode 2 problems: a request-size estimate that could keep refusing turns, and restored history that miscounted messages other plugins inject.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart OpenCode. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2 could refuse turns repeatedly when a request carried a reasoning setting or an inline image (#955):** OpenCode 2 adds an "effort" part when you pick a model variant, and it sends pasted images as "media" parts. Magic Context's request-size estimate didn't know either kind, so it marked the whole estimate as unreliable. When the history boundary also couldn't be placed, Magic Context then refused the turn without starting the recovery that would have summarized past it, and kept refusing until something unrelated rebuilt the history. An effort part now counts as zero tokens, since it selects a setting and carries no prompt text, and an inline image counts at its token cost, the same way image files already did. Requests themselves are unchanged.
- **Messages injected by other plugins counted as your own turns after a history restore on OpenCode 2 (#954):** OpenCode 2 stores messages that another plugin injects as their own kind of row. When Magic Context restored older history, it rebuilt those rows as ordinary user messages, so they counted as turns you had typed. That moved when old tool output was cleared, where the current turn started, and when reminders fired. Restored injected messages keep their marking now. What is sent to the provider is byte-for-byte the same.
